entries.test: Public development records, dated model evaluations, or disclosures establishing whether OpenAI had a completed GPT-5 by May 13, 2024, after fourteen months of development would settle this.
entries.note: The claim concerns possession of a developed model at publication, not merely whether it had been released.

entries.test: The contemporaneous OpenAI blogpost figure and its underlying results would establish the size of the differences between GPT-4o, GPT-4 Turbo, and GPT-4 on the displayed measures.
entries.note: The source ties the comparison to a particular figure. The normalization specifies benchmark performance generally, which the supplied text alone does not establish.

entries.test: Contemporaneous public GPT-4o error reports, including the cited Rosenzweig and Riley examples, and comparable reports about earlier models would establish whether numerous familiar errors were being reported.
entries.note: The source asserts that errors are being reported; the normalization strengthens this into an unqualified assertion that the model is producing them.
“Presumably” makes the causal explanation conjectural. “Had been predicted” also replaces the source’s hypothetical “would have predicted” with an actual prior prediction.
He presents the absence as evidence for a possibility, using “may have reached,” rather than firmly asserting diminishing returns.
